tasks.summary: Fixed the reviewer finding. relink-scan used to drop an action-query write silently when its SQL text was found but named no model table, because the table name was built at run time (a format placeholder or a concatenated variable). Such a write now gets an IDENTITY row ('any IDENTITY table', resolved from 'table name built at run time', SQL Server, add dbSeeChanges). It is also listed in a new '### Writes to tables named at run time' subsection under 'IDENTITY tables written from code', marked for both dialects, with a fix that says to confirm the write should still run after cutover and to list it in the cutover notes. The Summary table has a matching row. The engagement document was regenerated: modOrders.SetDatesToCurrent line 214 (Database.Execute, UPDATE) now appears in both places. identity_writes went from 42 to 43 and dynamic_writes is 1, so the change added no other rows. A hand-written fixture procedure covers both a concatenated and a placeholder table name, with and without dbSeeChanges, and has a new test. All 51 tests pass, every acceptance command exits 0 and the guard is clean.
notes: Root cause: in toolkit/relink.py, _identity_row treated 'SQL text found' as 'tables resolved'. Now SQL text that names no model table on a write that is not a SELECT counts as a write to a table named at run time. It is listed instead of dropped. When no SQL text is found at all, the scan still falls back to the procedure's references or 'not resolved', as before.

One existing assertion in test_identity_writes_with_and_without_dbseechanges was narrowed. It used to check that the word PostgreSQL appears nowhere in the IDENTITY section. It now checks only the main IDENTITY table, because the new subsection rightly names both dialects. The assertion is no looser: the main table must still be SQL Server only.

Cutover risk for both dialects: modOrders.SetDatesToCurrent shifts every date column in every non-system table. It can run at startup through modGlobal.OneTimeProcessing (a call from modStartup) and from the admin reset-dates subform. Once relinked, it would rewrite dates on the server on PostgreSQL as well as SQL Server, unless the first-run setting carried into the loaded data marks one-time processing as done. Assumption: the runbook and cutover templates must check that setting, or disable the routine, before users open the relinked front end. Question for the client: should the demo date-shift routine stay in the relinked front end at all?
The scanner does not trace call chains. The startup reachability above comes from the reviewer's evidence and a manual read of the model, not from the generated document.

issues.problem: The tests never show that --verify catches a foreign-key orphan or an identity that is not past the maximum. orphan_count is only ever exercised with 0 orphans. identity_problems and reset_identities return early on SQLite (the test engine), so they have no unit test at all. Both checks have run only on their passing path, in the real mp-data run (fk_orphans 0, no identity problems). A regression that stops either check from firing would not turn any test red.
issues.evidence: grep -n "orphan\|identity_problems\|not past the maximum\|reset_identities" toolkit/tests/test_stage1.py matches only lines 522 (asserts fk_orphans == 0) and 556 (key name). toolkit/stage1.py:993-995 `if d not in DIALECTS: return []` and stage1.py:872-874 skip SQLite. The verify run `mp-data --slot s3_review_r1_round1 stage1 ... --verify --require-rows --report ...` exited 0, with fk_orphans 0 on all 56 table entries.

issues.problem: --require-rows passes when the design and the dataset have no tables at all. require_rows_problems only flags 'every dataset table is empty' when `data` is non-empty, so a schema.json with zero data tables and a matching zero-table dataset loads 0 rows and exits 0. The contract says --require-rows exits 1 when every dataset table is empty, and that is vacuously true here.
issues.evidence: toolkit/stage1.py:1104 `if data and all(e["dataset_rows"] == 0 for e in data):`. With no entries, `data == []` and no problem is added. source_problems (stage1.py:729-744) adds nothing either when design.tables is empty.

issues.problem: stage1-frontend-changes.md says the Orders.OrderDate Now() default is "Not carried over" and tells the reader to set a CURRENT_TIMESTAMP server default. stage1 already creates that default. The Summary row "Validation rules and defaults not carried over | 4" counts it too, when only the 3 validation rules are left out. The runbook (item 8) correctly says stage1 creates the default, so the two client documents contradict each other. A DBA following frontend-changes could try to add a second default constraint, which SQL Server refuses.
issues.evidence: /home/cloudcli/sourcecode/access-excel-to-django/northwind/docs/stage1-frontend-changes.md line 170 ("Not carried over. Set a server default: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP on both servers.") and line 24 (count 4). /home/cloudcli/sourcecode/modernization-pipeline/toolkit/stage1.py lines 366-367 (default_clause returns sa.func.current_timestamp() for a Now() default on a datetime column). stage1-report.md's "Other objects not created" lists only the 3 validation rules and no default. /home/cloudcli/sourcecode/access-excel-to-django/northwind/docs/stage1-runbook.md line 113 ("stage1 creates a CURRENT_TIMESTAMP server default instead"). The wording comes from toolkit/relink.py lines 276 and 595-597, which do not use stage1.default_clause. relink-scan --check exits 0, so the file matches the generator: the defect is in the generator.

issues.problem: The cutover smoke checklist runs real order, purchase-order, receiving, stock-take and payment transactions on the live server database. It never says to use test records or to reverse or remove them afterwards, so production stock levels and order history change on cutover day. The "Dates unchanged" item then relies on the verify command's digests still matching. But the earlier checklist items have just added and changed rows in Orders, OrderDetails, PurchaseOrders, PurchaseOrderDetails, StockTake and Products, so the verify will report digest mismatches, and the check cannot be done as written.
issues.evidence: /home/cloudcli/sourcecode/access-excel-to-django/northwind/docs/stage1-cutover.md lines 59-61 (create, invoice, ship and pay an order; enter a stock take and reorder; create, approve and receive a PO so that stock rises), line 65 ("the verify command's digests still match unless people have entered rows"). No cleanup step appears in Smoke checklist, Rollback or Sign-off (lines 54-85). The template /home/cloudcli/sourcecode/modernization-pipeline/templates/docs/stage1-cutover.md lines 56-57 gives no guidance on test records either.
